page.layout: Top: two medallion portraits side by side, with their legends around the rims. Below them, one column of running text in full width, with a marginal reference at the right of the first paragraph's end. At the foot, a decorative ornament without text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: MENALIPPE,Orithyæ ac Antiopes(hæ ambæ Amazo-num reginæ erant)soror,ab Hercule bello superata,captiua ab-ducitur:quam tandem sorori reginæ reddit: & pretium , arma eiusdem reginæ (Baltheum fuisse dicũt)accipit:atque ita man-dato functus,ad Regem Eurystheum Hercules ipse,reuertitur. Vide Iustinum libr.2.

HIPPOLYTE, soror Orithyæ, Antiopes, & Menalip-pes, eodē ipso bello quo soror Menalippe ab Hercule capta,ac abducta est,hæc quoque à Thefeo capitur ac abducitur:Sed ta-men eam in vxorē Thefeus accipit, ex eáque gignit Hippoly-tum,vti iam à me dictum est supra,in Thefeo.Iustin.lib 2.
Nec verò nesciendū est, Hippolytum omnium castissimum fuisse,eundémque venationi deditissimū:de quo multa legere licet apud autores:maximè apud Ouidium li.15.Metamorpho item Heroidum epist.4.

page.notes: The two medallions carry legends around their rims. The left one reads MENALIPPE at the upper left and AMAZO at the right, partly obscured. The right one reads HIPPOL at the left and THESEI with a partly visible Greek or abbreviated ending at the right; the last letters are doubtful. The ornament at the bottom is a decorative block with no text. Two words are doubtful in the medallion legends and are marked [?].
